_meta.title: FDRS v2 formula regression fixtures
_meta.purpose: Pins the EXPECTED behaviour of the FDRS v2 score so any weight/amplifier change is caught. Each case has a 9-component vector and an expected score (clipped 0-100). Run with scripts/test_fdrs_v2.py.
_meta.formula: base = Sum(weight[i]*c[i]); amp = min(6*(c0/100)*(c7/100), 6); FDRS = clip(round(base+amp), 0, 100)

cases.name: high_import_high_econ_fragility
cases.desc: Import-dependent AND can't finance imports -> amplifier fires strongly. Should be high.

cases.name: high_import_low_econ_fragility
cases.desc: Import-dependent but can afford imports -> amplifier small. Should be lower than the high-fragility twin.

cases.name: low_import_high_econ_fragility
cases.desc: Poor but not import-dependent -> amplifier small (needs BOTH). Moderate score.
cases.assert: amplifier small despite high econ_access (import_dep gates it)

cases.name: resilient_exporter
cases.desc: Low import dependence, strong reserves, low fragility -> low score.

cases.name: all_max_clips_at_100
cases.desc: Max vector: base 100 + amp 6 = 106 -> MUST clip to 100. Validates the ceiling.

cases.name: missing_econ_access_no_amplifier
cases.desc: econ_access=0 -> amplifier is exactly 0 regardless of import_dep. Validates the calm-by-absence concern.
cases.assert: amplifier == 0 when econ_access == 0 (and note: this understates a real high-import country)

cases.name: missing_grain_buffer
cases.desc: grain_buffer=0 -> loses 0.06*value contribution only; no amplifier effect.

cases.name: unobserved_econ_access_skips_amplifier
cases.desc: v79. c7 is null (UNOBSERVED, not a sourced zero). The amplifier is an interaction between two measured quantities, so with one missing it is not computable and is skipped; the base renormalises over the 0.88 of weight actually observed. Contrast with missing_econ_access_no_amplifier above: an identical-looking vector carrying a REAL zero scores 61. That 8-point gap is the entire point — a country genuinely free of economic-access risk is not the same as a country we know nothing about, and the unknown one must never look safer.
cases.assert: null c7 scores HIGHER than real-zero c7 (61) — absence is not resilience

cases.name: unobserved_tail_renormalised
cases.desc: v79. The Aruba shape: c6/c7/c8 all unobserved, so only 0.82 of the weight is observed. Under the old missing-as-zero rule this scored 38 and looked calmer than a fully-sourced country at identical real risk; renormalising over observed weight gives 42.
cases.assert: renormalised over observed weight (was 38 under missing-as-zero)

cases.name: only_one_component_observed
cases.desc: v79. Degenerate case: a single observed component renormalises to itself. Guards the divide-by-observed-weight path against returning a diluted score when coverage is minimal.
cases.assert: single observed component renormalises to its own value

cases.name: all_unobserved_returns_zero
cases.desc: v79. No observed weight at all -> the formula cannot produce a score. Returns 0 as a sentinel rather than dividing by zero; consumers gate on completeness before displaying it.
cases.assert: zero observed weight returns 0 without dividing by zero
